+# Numeric generator identity costs
+
+`score.py` streams deterministic rewards for synthetic trajectory errors, then
+accumulates a total, second moment and threshold count. Its `typed` mode consumes
+raw float yields; `observed` passes the generator through `Any`, so each yielded
+object becomes observable. The `typed-alias` and `observed-alias` controls repeatedly
+yield one source number. All modes remain executable with CPython.
+
+From the repository root:
+
+```sh
+python3.13 bench/generator_identity/score.py typed 100000 5
+./pystachy build bench/generator_identity/score.py -o /tmp/generator-score
+/tmp/generator-score typed 100000 5
+/tmp/generator-score observed 100000 5
+/tmp/generator-score typed-alias 100000 5
+/tmp/generator-score observed-alias 100000 5
+```
+
+Each output line contains a checksum and the in-process duration in seconds.
+Compare checksums with CPython before interpreting timings. Use separate processes,
+interleave baseline/candidate order, and report build, whole-process JIT startup
+and steady execution separately. The fresh-expression control must not be used to
+claim that yielding an existing local or copying a default avoids boxing.
+
+For deterministic allocation counts, build separate AOT binaries with
+`PYSTACHY_CFLAGS=-DPYSTACHY_PROFILE_DATA` and private `PYSTACHY_CACHE` directories.
+The `pystachy-data` stderr record reports C allocation requests, requested bytes and
+managed-heap peak. These counters exclude foreign allocations and are not live
+memory or RSS. Keep their instrumented timings separate from ordinary timings.
+Ordinary no-Any and isolated nontracking generator IR are structural controls.
+
+## Allocation qualification
+
+Linux x86-64, CPython 3.13.16, LLVM 18.1.3; one instrumented AOT process per row,
+three repetitions of 20,000 scores. Every checksum matched CPython. The baseline
+is main `5f81cc25`; the eager implementation is `e0f17211` (the initial #1486).
+The companion implementation uses the code accompanying this workload.
+
+| Consumer | Main allocation requests | Eager yields | Nullable companions |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| Typed, fresh expression | 21 | 60,021 | 21 |
+| Any, fresh expression | 60,027 | 60,027 | 60,027 |
+| Typed, repeated source alias | 21 | 24 | 24 |
+| Any, repeated source alias | 60,027 | 30 | 30 |
+
+Fresh typed consumption returns to the baseline allocation count; actual dynamic
+observers still materialize objects. Repeated source aliases need one canonical
+box per generator invocation. Main's repeated-Any case allocates new boxes because
+it loses the source identity; it is a negative control, not equivalent semantics.
+For the typed fresh case, managed-heap peaks were 393,216 / 1,310,720 / 393,216
+bytes, respectively. Requested bytes include coroutine storage and formatted output
+and are not a reachable-memory census.
+
+Five interleaved uninstrumented processes per mode, each with five samples of
+200,000 scores, were pinned to one CPU during other qualification work. Median
+in-process AOT durations (main / eager / companion) were 11.37 / 12.81 / 9.80 ms
+for typed fresh scores and 12.57 / 12.24 / 12.89 ms for actual Any observation.
+These shared-host timings establish no general speedup. Warm CPython-hosted AOT
+builds took 1.79 / 1.71 / 1.79 s; whole-process CPython-hosted JIT runs of 20,000
+scores took 0.258 / 0.267 / 0.315 s. Startup is distinct from steady execution and
+remains a cost to qualify; instrumented durations were excluded.
+
+Reproduce each row by building the three source revisions with the flags above,
+then running the corresponding mode with arguments `20000 3`. The structural
+`tools/test_typed_generator_identity.py` control checks that a fresh-expression
+producer has no numeric boxing calls and fails when eager boxing is restored.

+# pystachy: dynamic-any
+"""Streaming reward scoring: typed reduction versus a dynamic observer."""
+import sys
+import time
+from typing import Any, Iterator
+
+
+def scores(count: int) -> Iterator[float]:
+    for i in range(count):
+        yield 1.0 / (1.0 + float((i * 73) % 97 - 48) ** 2 * 0.001)
+
+
+def aliases(count: int, score: float) -> Iterator[float]:
+    for _ in range(count):
+        yield score
+
+
+def typed(count: int, repeated: bool) -> float:
+    stream = aliases(count, float("0.25")) if repeated else scores(count)
+    total = 0.0
+    squares = 0.0
+    accepted = 0
+    for score in stream:
+        total += score
+        squares += score * score
+        if score >= 0.5:
+            accepted += 1
+    return total + squares + float(accepted)
+
+
+def observed(count: int, repeated: bool) -> float:
+    stream: Any = aliases(count, float("0.25")) if repeated else scores(count)
+    total = 0.0
+    squares = 0.0
+    accepted = 0
+    for item in stream:
+        score: float = item
+        total += score
+        squares += score * score
+        if score >= 0.5:
+            accepted += 1
+    return total + squares + float(accepted)
+
+
+mode = sys.argv[1]
+count = int(sys.argv[2])
+for _ in range(int(sys.argv[3])):
+    start = time.perf_counter()
+    answer = observed(count, mode == "observed-alias") if mode.startswith("observed") else typed(count, mode == "typed-alias")
+    print(answer, time.perf_counter() - start)

+# Numeric tuple identity costs
+
+`score.py` constructs two-item reward batches from fresh arithmetic. `typed`
+consumes only their scalar payloads; `observed` passes items through Any; `copy`
+slices a fresh tuple before observing either source item. All three modes have
+the same checksum and remain executable with CPython.
+
+```sh
+python3.13 bench/tuple_identity/score.py typed 20000 3
+./pystachy build bench/tuple_identity/score.py -o /tmp/tuple-score
+/tmp/tuple-score typed 20000 3
+/tmp/tuple-score observed 20000 3
+/tmp/tuple-score copy 20000 3
+```
+
+Each line contains the checksum and in-process duration in seconds. Compare
+checksums before timing; interleave parent/candidate binaries on the same idle
+core. Report whole-process JIT startup and AOT compilation separately. To compare
+ordinary programs, remove only the first pragma and the `Any` annotation/import:
+this requires a distinct source and must be reported as such.
+
+Use `PYSTACHY_CFLAGS=-DPYSTACHY_PROFILE_DATA` and private `PYSTACHY_CACHE`
+directories for deterministic AOT allocation requests and requested bytes.
+Instrumented timings are not ordinary performance results; counters exclude
+foreign allocation and are not RSS or live retention. Expect an eight-byte header
+increase for every runtime-length tuple. Identity-tracking numeric tuples also
+allocate a companion array; copies may materialize every fresh item box before
+sharing, even without an Any observation. `make listprobe` checks ownership,
+scan kinds, fresh-copy identity and positive/negative collection controls.
+
+## Allocation sample
+
+On 2026-11-14, x86-64 Linux, LLVM 18 and CPython 3.13.16, AOT builds at the
+default optimization tier 2 compared parent `7e96403e` with published candidate
+`2b00207e`. The tested candidate `34032b0e` has the same tree as that published
+commit. The parent native compiler came from the identical source tree
+`88c89982`; the candidate used the hosted compiler. Each build used the profiling flag above and a private
+runtime cache. One repetition of 20,000 batches returned `249830.375` in every
+mode, matching CPython. These are total requests, including startup and output:
+
+| Source | Mode | Allocations, parent → candidate | Requested bytes, parent → candidate |
+|---|---|---:|---:|
+| Dynamic Any | typed | 20,010 → 40,010 | 480,372 → 1,120,371 |
+| Dynamic Any | observed | 60,010 → 80,010 | 1,080,375 → 1,720,374 |
+| Dynamic Any | copy | 40,010 → 120,010 | 800,370 → 2,520,370 |
+| Ordinary | typed | 20,007 → 20,007 | 480,328 → 640,326 |
+| Ordinary | observed | 20,007 → 20,007 | 480,331 → 640,330 |
+| Ordinary | copy | 40,007 → 40,007 | 800,327 → 1,120,326 |
+
+The ordinary variant removes the pragma and `Any` import and changes `number`'s
+parameter to `float`. Its extra bytes correspond to the eight-byte tuple header;
+it makes no additional allocation requests. The dynamic typed mode adds one
+companion allocation per tuple, while the copy mode also materializes both fresh
+numeric items before sharing their identities. Thus preserving raw numeric
+storage does not make identity preservation allocation-free. Startup paths and
+printed output account for small byte differences beyond the tuple costs.
+
+[Raw counters and provenance](results/2026-11-14-allocations.json) include zero-count
+controls. This shared-host run supports allocation comparisons only; it makes no
+wall-time performance claim.

+# pystachy: dynamic-any
+"""Numeric tuple reward batches with optional identity observation and copies."""
+import sys
+import time
+from typing import Any
+
+
+def number(value: Any) -> float:
+    return value
+
+
+def score(count: int, mode: str) -> float:
+    total = 0.0
+    for i in range(count):
+        values: tuple[float, ...] = (float(i % 97) * 0.125, float(i % 53) * 0.25)
+        if mode == "copy":
+            tail = values[1:]
+            total += tail[0] + values[0]
+        elif mode == "observed":
+            total += number(values[0]) + number(values[1])
+        else:
+            total += values[0] + values[1]
+    return total
+
+
+mode = sys.argv[1]
+count = int(sys.argv[2])
+for _ in range(int(sys.argv[3])):
+    start = time.perf_counter()
+    answer = score(count, mode)
+    print(answer, time.perf_counter() - start)

@@ -0,0 +1,90 @@
+Pystachy v0.5.0-alpha.3 expands numeric protocols, complex numbers and container keys,
+adds a bounded Decimal implementation, and improves generic constructors and numeric
+identity across typed and dynamic code. It remains an experimental compiler for a typed
+subset of Python.
+
+## Constructors and value identity
+
+Classes with fixed field layouts can specialize their constructors independently,
+including supported inheritance hierarchies and imported constructor dependencies.
+Generic class checks agree across typed code, dynamic `Any` and helpers that do not
+opt in. Unused classes retain lazy validation.
+[#1493](https://github.com/den-run-ai/pystachy/pull/1493),
+[generic classes](https://github.com/den-run-ai/pystachy/blob/v0.5.0-alpha.3/docs/language/typing.md#class-templates-and-generic-classes)
+
+Numeric generator yields and runtime-length tuple items preserve their identities when
+crossing into dynamic `Any`. Optional numeric lists and tuples preserve the corresponding
+identities as well. The compiler records these companion reads and writes for its storage
+checks; typed yields avoid allocating an identity box until a consumer needs one.
+[#1486](https://github.com/den-run-ai/pystachy/pull/1486),
+[#1491](https://github.com/den-run-ai/pystachy/pull/1491),
+[boundary contract](https://github.com/den-run-ai/pystachy/blob/v0.5.0-alpha.3/docs/dynamic-any.md)
+
+## Numeric protocols and Decimal
+
+Objects can supply the supported conversion and rounding methods used by `int()`,
+`float()`, `round()`, `math.floor()`, `math.ceil()` and `math.trunc()`. Builtin numbers
+on the left can call supported reflected arithmetic methods, including IntEnum and
+IntFlag members. Comparison methods can decline with `NotImplemented`, allowing the
+next comparison candidate to run in Python's order.
+[#1340](https://github.com/den-run-ai/pystachy/pull/1340),
+[#1426](https://github.com/den-run-ai/pystachy/pull/1426),
+[#1472](https://github.com/den-run-ai/pystachy/pull/1472)
+
+Combined comparison checks cover declining user methods, nullable enum receivers and
+Decimal/complex equality, including exact comparisons with the real float component.
+
+The new `decimal` subset supports exact construction from strings, integers and floats;
+context-rounded arithmetic; comparisons; hashing; formatting; `quantize()`; `sqrt()`;
+integer powers; and all eight rounding modes. `Context`, `getcontext()` and
+`localcontext()` expose the supported precision, rounding and exponent settings.
+[#1341](https://github.com/den-run-ai/pystachy/pull/1341),
+[library limits](https://github.com/den-run-ai/pystachy/blob/v0.5.0-alpha.3/lib/compatibility.md)
+
+Decimal signal flags and configurable traps, transcendental functions, construction from
+another Decimal, Decimal subclasses and `sum()` of Decimals remain unsupported. General
+reflected arithmetic between two user objects and unrestricted uses of the
+`NotImplemented` value remain outside this subset.
+
+## Complex numbers
+
+Imaginary literals, `complex()` and complex annotations work with arithmetic,
+comparison, hashing, absolute values and formatting. Complex values also participate
+in supported closed scalar unions and dynamic `Any`, with identities retained across
+those boundaries. Arithmetic follows the CPython 3.13 algorithms, including their
+IEEE exceptional values.
+[#1408](https://github.com/den-run-ai/pystachy/pull/1408),
+[#1409](https://github.com/den-run-ai/pystachy/pull/1409),
+[#1421](https://github.com/den-run-ai/pystachy/pull/1421)
+
+Ordering, floor division, modulo, attribute assignment and `sum()` of complex numbers
+remain unsupported. Equal complex literals can be distinct objects, as documented;
+the `cmath` module is not included.
+
+## Container keys
+
+Sets and dictionaries accept `None` and supported optional key types. Runtime-length
+tuples of supported scalar items can be keys, and equal fixed and runtime-length tuples
+find the same entry. Unions of ordinary classes can be keys when all possible classes
+use identity hashing and equality.
+[#1412](https://github.com/den-run-ai/pystachy/pull/1412),
+[#1467](https://github.com/den-run-ai/pystachy/pull/1467),
+[#1475](https://github.com/den-run-ai/pystachy/pull/1475)
+
+Optional fixed-shape tuple keys preserve promoting integers through set algebra and
+dictionary operations. Mixed object sets consistently support removing and discarding
+`None`; missing `None` keys produce `KeyError` without dereferencing an absent object.
+
+## Verification, limits and platforms
+
+Expanded Lean boundary checks validate emitted class layouts, selected alias preservation
+and collector trace edges, and numeric identity companions. These bounded models do not
+prove general aliasing or collector correctness. Dynamic `Any` and promoting integers
+remain experimental opt-ins; async, full native mypy and broad concurrency remain outside
+this release.
+[Verification scope](https://github.com/den-run-ai/pystachy/blob/v0.5.0-alpha.3/tools/lean_boundary/README.md)
+
+Native archives target Linux x86-64/AArch64 with glibc 2.39+ and LLVM 18, and macOS
+arm64/x86-64 with macOS 15+, Xcode Command Line Tools and LLVM 20. Linux archives
+are not manylinux packages. Archives and Docker run without Python; the hosted compiler

+loads this module for a program that may use one (Loader.program); programs do not import it, it
+runs no code, and its functions are compiled where a program uses them. The compiler passes each
+operand of an operation as its two floats, an int or a float x as (float(x), 0.0), as CPython's

+### `decimal`
+
+`decimal` is a subset implementation (`lib/decimal.py`) that opts in to
+[promoting ints](../docs/python-int.md) for its coefficients. `Decimal` values are exact when
+constructed and rounded to the current context by arithmetic, with CPython's results, text,
+hashes and messages for the supported API
+([API walk](../tests/programs/library/lib_decimal.py),
+[operand grid](../tests/programs/library/lib_decimal_grid.py),
+[typed program data](../tests/programs/library/lib_decimal_records.py)).
+
+Supported: construction from `str`, `int` and `float`; `+ - * / // %`, `divmod()`, integer
+`**`, unary operators and `abs()`, with a `Decimal` or an `int` on either side; comparison with
+a `Decimal`, `int` or `float`; equality with a `complex` number (comparing its real part's
+exact float value when the imaginary part is zero); `hash()`, `int()`, `float()`, `round()`, `math.floor()`,
+`math.ceil()`, `math.trunc()`, `bool()`, `str()`, `repr()` and `format()`; `quantize()`,
+`to_integral_value()`, `normalize()`, `sqrt()`, `fma()`, `remainder_near()`, `scaleb()`,
+`compare()`, `max()`, `min()`, the `is_*()`, `copy_*()` and `as_*()` methods; `Context`,
+`getcontext()`, `setcontext()`, `localcontext()` and the three predefined contexts; all eight
+rounding modes; NaNs, infinities and signed zeros.
+
+Comparisons decline operands outside these numeric types so that their reflected
+comparison methods run, including in tuple searches. Direct comparison-method calls
+that could return `NotImplemented` retain the compiler's
+[bounded comparison contract](../docs/language/semantics.md#object-protocols).
+
+- **Signals.** Flags are not recorded and traps are fixed at the default:
+  `InvalidOperation`, `DivisionByZero` and `Overflow` always raise, and the other signals
+  never do. `Context` has no `flags` or `traps`, and its `repr()` shows none set.
+- **Exception classes.** A class has one exception base here: `DivisionByZero` derives from
+  `ZeroDivisionError` but not from `DecimalException`; `Overflow` and `Underflow` derive from
+  `Inexact` but not from `Rounded` (or `Subnormal`); `FloatOperation` is not a `TypeError`.
+- **Constructor.** `Decimal(d)` of a `Decimal`, `Decimal(True)` and
+  `Decimal((sign, digits, exponent))` are compile-time errors: use the value itself, or `+d`
+  to round it to the context.
+- **Powers and logarithms.** The exponent of `**` is an `int`; `exp()`, `ln()`, `log10()`,
+  `logb()`, the logical and shifting operations, `next_minus()`, `next_plus()`,
+  `next_toward()`, `compare_total()` and `compare_signal()` are not provided, and
+  `int ** Decimal` is not supported.
+- **Integers beyond 64 bits.** `int()`, `round()`, `math.floor()` and `as_integer_ratio()`
+  return large integers to a module that opts in to promoting ints
+  ([test](../tests/programs/library/lib_decimal_python_int.py)) and raise `OverflowError` in
+  one that does not. An `int` given to the constructor or to an operator is a 64-bit value:
+  pass a larger one as text.
+- **Typing.** `sum()` of Decimals is not supported: add them in a loop. `Decimal` cannot be
+  subclassed. A NaN hashes to 0, and one context is shared by all threads.
+- **Formatting.** The `n` type uses the C locale's format, and a value whose coefficient has
+  more than 4,300 digits cannot be converted to text.

+                 clamp: int | None = None) -> _ContextManager:
+    """A context manager whose block runs with a copy of ctx (the current context by default)."""
+    new = (getcontext() if ctx is None else ctx).copy()
+    if prec is not None:
+        new.prec = prec
+    if rounding is not None:
+        new.rounding = rounding
+    if Emin is not None:
+        new.Emin = Emin
+    if Emax is not None:
+        new.Emax = Emax
+    if capitals is not None:
+        new.capitals = capitals
+    if clamp is not None:
+        new.clamp = clamp

+def _ndigits(n: int) -> int:
+    # the number of decimal digits of n >= 0 (1 for 0), without the text of a large n
+    if n < 10:
+        return 1
+    d = n.bit_length() * 1233 >> 12
+    while n >= 10 ** d:
+        d += 1
+    while n < 10 ** (d - 1):
+        d -= 1
+    return d
+
+
+def _round_changed(sign: int, q: int, r: int, half: int, keep: int, rounding: str) -> int:
+    # which way rounding moves a coefficient cut into quotient q and remainder r (half is half a
+    # unit of q's last place; keep is the number of digits q keeps): 1 up, 0 exact, -1 down
+    down = 0 if r == 0 else -1
+    if rounding == ROUND_HALF_EVEN:
+        if r == half and (keep == 0 or q % 2 == 0):
+            return -1
+        return 1 if r >= half else down
+    if rounding == ROUND_HALF_UP:
+        return 1 if r >= half else down
+    if rounding == ROUND_DOWN:
+        return down
+    if rounding == ROUND_UP:
+        return -down
+    if rounding == ROUND_HALF_DOWN:
+        if r == half:
+            return -1
+        return 1 if r >= half else down
+    if rounding == ROUND_CEILING:
+        return down if sign else -down
+    if rounding == ROUND_FLOOR:
+        return -down if sign else down
+    if rounding == ROUND_05UP:

+        return -down

+    def _parse(self, value: str) -> None:

+        n = len(text)
+        if i < n and (text[i] == "-" or text[i] == "+"):
+            self._sign = 1 if text[i] == "-" else 0
+            i += 1
+        rest = text[i:].lower()

+            self._kind = _INFINITY

+        if rest.startswith("nan") or rest.startswith("snan"):
+            diag = rest[3:] if rest.startswith("nan") else rest[4:]
+            if diag != "" and not diag.isdecimal():

+            self._kind = _NAN if rest.startswith("nan") else _SNAN
+            self._int = int(diag) if diag != "" else 0

+        while i < n and text[i].isdecimal():
+            i += 1
+        intpart = text[start:i]
+        fracpart = ""
+        if i < n and text[i] == ".":
+            i += 1
+            start = i
+            while i < n and text[i].isdecimal():

+            fracpart = text[start:i]

+        if i < n and (text[i] == "e" or text[i] == "E"):
+            i += 1
+            start = i
+            if i < n and (text[i] == "-" or text[i] == "+"):

+# What one method returns is kept apart from what the comparisons it runs return: a method that
+# compares objects whose methods return NotImplemented, and then returns a result of its own;
+# and one that returns NotImplemented after a comparison that gave a result.
+class Inner:
+    def __init__(self, n: int) -> None:
+        self.n = n
+
+    def __eq__(self, other):
+        print("Inner.__eq__", self.n)
+        if not isinstance(other, Inner) or other.n < 0 or self.n < 0:
+            return NotImplemented
+        return self.n == other.n

+class Outer:
+    def __init__(self, a: int, b: int) -> None:
+        self.a = Inner(a)
+        self.b = Inner(b)

+        print("Outer.__eq__")
+        if not isinstance(other, Outer):
+            return NotImplemented

+# int() and float() of an object ask its own class: a derived class that defines __int__ or
+# __float__ where its base has __index__, or no method at all, is converted by its own
+# method through a base-typed reference, and a class that has none raises TypeError.
+class Base:
+    def __index__(self) -> int:
+        return 3
+
+
+class Child(Base):
+    def __int__(self) -> int:
+        return 9
+
+    def __float__(self) -> float:
+        return 9.5
+
+
+class Grand(Child):
+    def __int__(self) -> int:
+        return 27
+
+
+class Other(Base):
+    def __index__(self) -> int:
+        return 4
+
+
+class Plain:
+    def __init__(self, n: int) -> None:
+        self.n = n
+
+
+class Counted(Plain):
+    def __int__(self) -> int:
+        return self.n
+
+
+class Ratio(Plain):
+    def __float__(self) -> float:
+        return self.n / 2
+
+
+def show(x: Base) -> None:
+    print(int(x), float(x))
+
+
+def whole(x: Plain) -> None:
+    try:
+        print(int(x))
+    except TypeError as e:
+        print("TypeError:", e)
+
+
+def real(x: Plain) -> None:
+    try:
+        print(float(x))
+    except TypeError as e:
+        print("TypeError:", e)
+
+
+def pick(n: int) -> Base:
+    return [Base(), Child(), Grand(), Other()][n]
+
+
+for i in range(4):
+    show(pick(i))
+for p in [Plain(1), Counted(5), Ratio(7)]:
+    whole(p)
+    real(p)
+none: Base = pick(0) if len("x") > 1 else None
+try:
+    print(int(none))
+except TypeError as e:
+    print("TypeError:", e)
+try:
+    print(float(none))
+except TypeError as e:
+    print("TypeError:", e)

+# int(o) calls o.__int__(), else o.__index__(); float(o) calls o.__float__(), else o.__index__();
+# round(o) and round(o, n) call o.__round__, a template whose result each call types; math.floor(o),
+# math.ceil(o) and math.trunc(o) call o.__floor__(), o.__ceil__() and o.__trunc__(). The calls
+# dispatch on the object's class, evaluate their arguments first, and None raises CPython's TypeError.
+import math
+
+
+class Money:
+    def __init__(self, cents: int) -> None:
+        self.cents = cents
+
+    def __int__(self) -> int:
+        print("Money.__int__")
+        return self.cents // 100
+
+    def __float__(self) -> float:
+        return self.cents / 100
+
+    def __round__(self, ndigits=None):
+        if ndigits is None:
+            return (self.cents + 50) // 100
+        return Money(self.cents - self.cents % 10 ** (2 - ndigits))
+
+    def __floor__(self) -> int:
+        return self.cents // 100
+
+    def __ceil__(self) -> int:
+        return -(-self.cents // 100)
+
+    def __trunc__(self) -> int:
+        return int(self.cents / 100)
+
+    def __repr__(self) -> str:
+        return "Money(%d)" % self.cents
+
+
+class Debt(Money):
+    def __int__(self) -> int:
+        print("Debt.__int__")
+        return -(self.cents // 100)
+
+    def __float__(self) -> float:
+        return -1.5
+
+
+class Slot:
+    def __index__(self) -> int:
+        return 7
+
+
+class Fixed:
+    def __round__(self, ndigits: int = 0) -> int:
+        return 40 + ndigits
+
+
+def show(m: Money) -> None:
+    print(int(m), float(m), round(m), round(m, 1), round(m, None), math.floor(m), math.ceil(m), math.trunc(m))
+
+
+def arg(tag: str, m: Money) -> Money:
+    print("arg", tag)
+    return m
+
+
+show(Money(1234))
+show(Money(-1234))
+show(Debt(1234))
+print(int(Slot()), float(Slot()), round(Fixed()), round(Fixed(), 2), round(Fixed(), None))
+print(int(arg("a", Money(250))) + int(arg("b", Debt(250))), [int(m) for m in [Money(100), Debt(250)]], [float(m) for m in [Money(100), Debt(250)]])
+print(type(int(Money(5))).__name__, type(float(Money(5))).__name__, type(round(Money(5))).__name__, type(round(Money(5), 1)).__name__)
+
+

+        elif which == 1:

+        elif which == 4:

+    except TypeError as error:
+        print("TypeError:", error)
+

+# number op object calls the object's reflected method (__radd__, __rsub__, ...): a builtin number
+# has no method for it. The operands are evaluated left to right before the call, the method is
+# dispatched on the object's class, and a None object raises CPython's TypeError.
+
+
+class Money:
+    def __init__(self, cents: int) -> None:
+        self.cents = cents
+
+    def __add__(self, other: int) -> "Money":
+        print("Money.__add__", other)
+        return Money(self.cents + other * 100)
+
+    def __radd__(self, other: int) -> "Money":
+        print("Money.__radd__", other)
+        return Money(self.cents + other * 100)
+
+    def __rsub__(self, other: int) -> "Money":
+        return Money(other * 100 - self.cents)
+
+    def __rmul__(self, other: int) -> "Money":
+        return Money(self.cents * other)
+
+    def __rtruediv__(self, other: float) -> float:
+        return other / (self.cents / 100)
+
+    def __rfloordiv__(self, other: int) -> int:
+        return other * 100 // self.cents
+
+    def __rmod__(self, other: int) -> int:
+        return other * 100 % self.cents
+
+    def __rand__(self, other: int) -> int:
+        return other & self.cents
+
+    def __ror__(self, other: int) -> int:
+        return other | self.cents
+
+    def __rxor__(self, other: int) -> int:
+        return other ^ self.cents
+
+    def __rlshift__(self, other: int) -> int:
+        return other << (self.cents % 8)
+
+    def __rrshift__(self, other: int) -> int:
+        return other >> (self.cents % 8)
+
+    def __repr__(self) -> str:
+        return "Money(%d)" % self.cents
+
+
+class Loud(Money):
+    def __radd__(self, other: int) -> "Money":
+        print("Loud.__radd__", other)
+        return Money(-1)
+
+
+class Ratio:
+    def __init__(self, value: float) -> None:
+        self.value = value
+
+    def __radd__(self, other: float) -> float:
+        return other + self.value
+
+    def __rmul__(self, other: int | float) -> float:
+        return other * self.value
+
+
+def left() -> int:
+    print("left")
+    return 2
+
+
+def right(m: Money) -> Money:
+    print("right")
+    return m
+
+
+def show(m: Money) -> None:
+    print(1 + m, 10 - m, 3 * m, 2.5 / m, 7 // m, 7 % m, m + 1)
+    print(6 & m, 8 | m, 5 ^ m, 1 << m, 1024 >> m)
+
+
+show(Money(250))
+show(Loud(250))
+print(left() + right(Money(5)))
+print(1.5 + Ratio(0.25), 2 * Ratio(1.5), 2.0 * Ratio(1.5), [n * Money(3) for n in range(3)])
+total = 0 + Money(1)
+total = 2 + total
+print(total)
+
+

+    m: Money | None = Money(1) if n == 0 else None
+    try:
+        print(1 + m)
+    except TypeError as error:
+        print("TypeError:", error)
+
+
+none_case(0)
+none_case(1)

+class Holder:
+    def __init__(self) -> None:

+
+    def mark(self) -> None:
+        self.flags.add(None)
+        self.names.add("n")

+
+
+def run(steps: list[bool]) -> Result[None]:
+    before: dict[tuple[str, int], set[None]] = {}
+    after: dict[tuple[str, int], set[None]] = {}
+    cur: set[None] = set()
+    for i in range(len(steps)):

+    for path, text in messages:

app.description:
Codecov provides highly integrated tools to group, merge, archive and compare coverage reports. Whether your team is comparing changes in a pull request or reviewing a single commit, Codecov will improve the code review workflow and quality.

## Code coverage done right.®

1. Upload coverage reports from your CI builds.
2. Codecov merges all builds and languages into one beautiful coherent report.
3. Get commit statuses, pull request comments and coverage overlay via our browser extension.

When Codecov merges your uploads it keeps track of the CI provider (inc. build details) and user specified context, e.g. `#unittest` ~ `#smoketest` or `#oldcode` ~ `#newcode`. You can track the `#unittest` coverage independently of other groups. [Learn more here](
http://docs.codecov.io/docs/flags)

Through **Codecov's Browser Extension** reports overlay directly in GitHub UI to assist in code review in [Chrome](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/codecov/gedikamndpbemklijjkncpnolildpbgo) or Firefox (https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/codecov/)

*Highly detailed* **pull request comments** and *customizable* **commit statuses** will improve your team's workflow and code coverage incrementally.

**File backed configuration** all through the `codecov.yml`. 

## FAQ
- Do you **merge multiple uploads** to the same commit? **Yes**
- Do you **support multiple languages** in the same project? **Yes**
- Can you **group coverage reports** by project and/or test type? **Yes**
- How does **pricing** work? Only paid users can view reports and post statuses/comments.
